label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L=3-5), boosted by first token k/l/r/d/w/y
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (99% of activation mass; it never fires in the copy phase), and only when the sequence is short. When L=3 it fires on nearly every <DEL>, when L=4 on about half, when L=5 on about 13%, and when L>=6 almost never. Within L=4-5, whether it fires depends on the first original token, i.e. the token about to be output: k, l, r, d, w and y give the highest rates, then a, b, h, 2, s and v, while z, i, o, u, m and p rarely fire. The largest activations are on L=3 sequences starting with k. Weak residual firing (about 1% of mass) on the last original input of short sequences (t=2-4), mostly tokens j, 1 and z. (phase==1)&(L<=4) alone gives dev F1 0.68 and mass recall 0.89. The first-token gating raises F1 to 0.76, but the cutoff stays graded rather than sharp.
